knownRisks.ecrThrottle: The beta.37 max run lost 3 datacurve cells pre-model to a public.ecr.aws pull throttle (`429 toomanyrequests: Data limit exceeded`) while building 8 images concurrently. The condition is kept at fh_max_parallel=8 for fidelity with the source formal run, so the throttle may recur. If it does, those cells are pre-model environment failures and are recoverable through the repository's recovery channel (exactly as batch recovery-no-prediction-20260927 recovered the beta.37 ones).
knownRisks.perCallCeiling: polyglot-c-py and regex-log errored twice at reasoning effort max because their first model call outran the CLI's own --model-timeout-ms 840000 ceiling (measured 840.021s/840.022s and 840.021s/840.026s in two independent dispatches). The timeout pipeline is byte-identical in beta.38, so the same outcome is expected. If it recurs, the cells stay verdict-less, the run stays not scoreable, and per the repository's rules nothing is retried: only an explicitly authorized change to the per-call ceiling or to the effort condition could give those cells a verdict, and neither is made here.

outcomeDetail.budgetExhaustion: 9 attempts used their whole declared agent budget and were killed at that edge (meriyah 5571s/5400s, build-cython-ext 939/900, chess-best-move 938/900, code-from-image 1230/1200, dna-insert 1835/1800, extract-elf 949/900, gcode-to-text 934/900, largest-eigenval 935/900, sanitize-git-repo 935/900); all 9 carry failed verdicts and none still passed (beta.37: 10, of which 2 still passed). measuredCallDurations.finding: Model-call latency still dominates the wall clock (83-97% on almost every cell), so harness-side time is not the lever. At max effort a single call can reach 1206.7s, two first calls exceed the CLI's own 840s ceiling, and 9 cells die at their budget edge; the max condition buys longer calls, not more verdicts, and in this run it produced the same 14/11/5 ledger as beta.37.

conclusion: The full-corpus max-effort run on the newest candidate is again not scoreable: 5 of 30 cells carry no verdict (3 pre-model public.ecr.aws pull throttles, 2 single calls that hit the CLI's own 840s per-call ceiling), so verdicts.complete failed and passAt1 is null. Both failure modes this manifest pre-declared in knownRisks reproduced, and 4 of the 5 verdict-less tasks are the same as in the beta.37 max run. On the 25 valid cells the pass rate is 56.0% (14 of 25) against the source run's 63.3% at effort high, and the direct task comparison is 14 of 30 against 19 of 30; the ledger (14/11/5, 46.7%) is identical to beta.37's, with 5 cells flipped in each direction individually. The mechanically repeatable effect of the effort condition remains latency, not capability: 9 cells died at their own budget edge, one call reached 1206.7s, and two first calls exceeded the client-side per-call ceiling. Because beta.37 -> beta.38 carries exactly one model-visible change (the thread tools' v2 invocation schema), none of this is a code effect; it is that small delta plus run-to-run variance. Nothing was altered to make the run scoreable, and no recovery was dispatched: the three pre-model environment cells would be admissible for the repository's recovery channel, but only under the user's explicit authorization, and the two per-call-timeout cells have now failed to produce a verdict in two independent measurements.
